decisions.statement: Modify `parse_list_literal_or_comprehension` to avoid exponential backtracking on nested `[(...)]` lists by only attempting pattern comprehension where it can succeed via bracket counting and skipping already-failed attempts via memoization.
Unicode string unescaping now strictly requires all 4 or 8 characters to be ASCII hex digits before parsing, rejecting leading plus signs.
The lexer's whitespace skipping function now treats carriage return '\r' as whitespace in accordance with the openCypher grammar.
decisions.note: parity decision: matches existing behaviour (the C engine or openCypher) rather than a new choice

decisions.statement: Lexer::read_spaces was rewritten to end block comments only at */, treat any other / as division, and properly handle unterminated block comments or trailing slashes to match the C engine and openCypher.

Correct hand-written parser rules in graph/src/parser/cypher.rs to align with the openCypher grammar and C engine behavior regarding NOT runs, IS NULL predicate chains, expression lists, SET and REMOVE targets, MATCH MATCH syntax, and LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS.
The parser uses a ForbiddenPatternComprehension error enum to reject pattern comprehensions in inline property maps, MERGE ON CREATE/ON MATCH SET clauses, and index OPTIONS.
Parse parameter values directly into Value instances rather than building an intermediate expression tree.
The lexer error formatter cuts error contexts to an 80-byte window around the error position instead of embedding the entire query string.
Parser expression descent and tree depths are bounded by a MAX_TREE_DEPTH limit of 256 to prevent stack overflow crashes on deeply nested queries.
The identifier parser provides a non-allocating try_parse_ident method returning an Option for speculative call sites.
Enforce a maximum value nesting depth of 4,096 levels on entry where nested values enter storage, RDB decode, property writes, and bulk inserts.
Enforce unique constraints by looking up each written entity's values in the constraint's supporting index instead of scanning the label once per entity.
The native index is updated once per unit of work rather than once per graph write call.
The binder drops the Paren wrapper and flattens nested associative operations during expression binding.
Replace the multi-pass self-loop reordering loop with a single-pass function named hop_order::self_loops_after_binders.
Emit the body's entry projection unconditionally for every CALL {} subquery, projecting nothing when nothing is imported.
The team uses samply as the profiling tool for finding performance bottlenecks in the codebase.
Move the toolchain and all referencing components from LLVM 22 to LLVM 23 to resolve profile format version mismatches in coverage jobs.
Migrate the default development branch to the Rust implementation of FalkorDB while keeping the C engine maintained and released from master.
The native index is updated once per unit of work rather than once per graph write call.
Claim the MVCC write slot at escalation rather than at the start of a queued write.
Call self.resize() in get_type_id_mut after registering the type so relationship_type_matrix width stays synchronized with relationship_types.len().

Parse module-load arguments in graph_init using a single unified parser instead of two separate parsers, making option names ASCII case-insensitive, rejecting odd argument counts and unknown names, and applying load-only rules or GRAPH.CONFIG validators.
Runs redis-server in the Docker image as the unprivileged falkordb user instead of root using gosu.
Rust now saves virtual keys as graphmeta, the type C uses, so that C keeps graphs in GRAPH.LIST during a downgrade.

cypher.cypher:
// 10 F8 impact radius: what usually changes together with $module, the active decisions
// that affect those modules, and who knows them best (top EXPERT_IN).
// Decisions below $min_confidence (DECISION_MIN_CONFIDENCE) are left out, as everywhere.
// share = count / commits that touched $module under the same filter as the derive job
// (not bulk, <= $max_modules modules), e.g. "half of parser commits also touch planner".
MATCH (m:Module {id: $module})<-[:TOUCHES]-(c:Commit)-[:TOUCHES]->(x:Module)
WHERE NOT coalesce(c.bulk, false)
WITH m, c, count(x) AS k
WITH m, sum(CASE WHEN k <= $max_modules THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS base
MATCH (m)-[r:CO_CHANGED]-(n:Module)
WHERE r.count >= $min_count
OPTIONAL MATCH (d:Decision {status: 'active'})-[:AFFECTS]->(n)
WHERE d.confidence >= $min_confidence
WITH m, base, n, r, collect(DISTINCT {id: d.id, statement: d.statement, kind: d.kind, source_url: d.source_url}) AS decisions
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Person)-[e:EXPERT_IN]->(n)
WITH base, n, r, decisions, p, e ORDER BY e.score DESC
WITH base, n, r, decisions,
     [x IN collect({id: p.id, person: coalesce(p.login, p.name), score: e.score}) WHERE x.person IS NOT NULL][0..3] AS experts
RETURN n.id AS module_id, n.path AS module, r.count AS count,
       CASE WHEN base > 0 THEN round(100.0 * r.count / base) ELSE 0 END AS share_pct,
       base AS module_commits,
       [x IN decisions WHERE x.id IS NOT NULL] AS decisions, experts
ORDER BY count DESC
LIMIT $limit

// 09 F5 triage: decisions that AFFECT any of $modules (the modules where similar issues were
// fixed), with status and kind so the tool can keep proposed and superseded ones apart from
// current ones. Decisions below $min_confidence are left out.
UNWIND $modules AS mid
MATCH (d:Decision)-[:AFFECTS]->(m:Module {id: mid})
WHERE d.confidence >= $min_confidence
WITH d, collect(DISTINCT m.id) AS modules
RETURN d.id AS id, d.statement AS statement, d.status AS status, d.kind AS kind,
       d.confidence AS confidence, d.source_id AS source_id, d.source_url AS source_url, modules
ORDER BY size(modules) DESC, d.valid_from DESC
LIMIT $limit
